metadata.description: Google Slides deck generation: template-driven, from-scratch, Scalar product and proposal workflows, plus draw.io diagrams, an optional visual-QA skill, PPTX export, and line-item spreadsheets (Excel / Google Spreadsheet) for estimates and BOMs, on a shared Python engine

plugins.name: slide-forge
plugins.description: Generate Google Slides decks with Python + the Slides API. Eight skills on one shared engine: google-slides-template (generate from a registered master template with interactive intake and spec validation), google-slides (from-scratch decks via a blank template spec path or a code-first deckkit path with offline layout validation), scalar-product-slides (Scalar Inc. company/product deck workflow), scalar-proposal-slides (customer-challenge-driven Scalar solution proposals with challenge-to-product mapping, 3-environment architecture diagrams, and a BOM with quantities and monthly costs), drawio-diagrams (dense cloud architecture / data-flow diagrams authored as draw.io files and exported to PNG headlessly), slide-qa (thumbnail-based visual QA of a generated deck — optional at generation time, default on, with cleanup of the local QA files when done), pptx-export (export a generated deck to PowerPoint .pptx as a delivery format — chosen at intake or run standalone on any deck URL, with automatic fallback past the 10MB export limit and archival in the deck's Drive folder), and spreadsheets (line-item Excel / Google Spreadsheet deliverables — estimates, BOMs, cost breakdowns — from one JSON spec with typed columns, real formulas for amounts and subtotal/tax/total, offline validation, and in-place updates that preserve the Spreadsheet URL; the companion to a proposal deck's cost slide). Includes charts, business-framework figures, pictogram and cloud-vendor icon libraries, AI image generation, and parallel per-page spec authoring for large decks. The /forge command runs the whole pipeline (skill routing → intake → outline approval → validation → generation → optional visual QA → cleanup → report) as one continuous flow.
